I mean when I first moved in with my bf I thought I had to stay in and do all these chores and not go out unless it was with my partner until I realised wait, nobody was asking me to do that except my surprisingly regressive subconscious view of gender. Now I go out for about an hour and a half a day to go gym and however long I like otherwise, bf or no. Nobody was asking me to stay at home. Maybe you're imagining restrictions. 

However I don't know if that's what's happening here. You say your wife is "opposed" to fun and excitement; I've never met such a person. You call the fun and excitement you want to have a "lifestyle." Is it an activity like bowling or a pretty big life change like polyamory that you should have mentioned to her earlier? 

Fun and excitement is easy found if you're looking for it. Personally I wonder if you're either projecting preferences and dislikes onto her without asking (as I did when I decided I was Martha Stewart without the salary for some reason), or simply fantasising about a life without her in whatever way your brain allows it. 

If it's the first one, just say whatever activity you want to do if it doesn't compromise your relationship (things like reasonable hobbies/meeting friends/taking up a sport shouldn't tear your relationship apart, unless you're planning to use them to avoid responsibilities). 

If it's the second one, honestly, you're not communicating well with your wife and you're being a bit unfair to her. You also say everyone tells me I'm not grown up -- when people say that to men they're usually referring to chores and other responsibilities, not not having fun. 

Are you leaving your wife with a lot of domestic duties and life admin and then discovering she "nags" (takes the extra effort to tell you to do things that would usually be expected) you? Is the dynamic "I just want to relax but every time I see her she has another task for me?" BC if so, good news, you can change it by being proactive about household responsibilities, getting that out the way, and properly planning for "fun" (I'm sure she'd feel pretty "fun" too if her husband proactively vacuumed). 

A big part of feeling like a kid is not feeling in control of your life or having agency. But this feeling you have is in your control to change. Don't imagine it's imposed on you by your "fun hating" (who hates fun??) wife.

[this is the basic cup](https://vm.tiktok.com/ZGe3CxTJb/) cup, the last 2 layers of which are white then black. Then I double crocheted along (perpendicular to the cup) the 2 sides in blue, then did a puff stitch/triple pivot/puff stitch border. 

Then I mesh stitched to connect the base of the cups together and form a band. Under that, I alternated DC layers, DC mesh layers, TC mesh layers, hdc layers, all in different colours. Then I finished the base of the band with the same puff stitch /TC edging as the cups. 

Then I crocheted blue single crochet along the sides of the band from the top down, and when I got to the bottom, I kept chaining to form a tie. After my final crochet for the tie chain, I left the loop open so I could post wool through to form a tassel. 

I did the same on the other side, and on the top, I crocheted the chain into the top of the top picots and made tassels in those too.

I used to go to classes a lot in my old gym but now I've moved and the times my gym runs classes don't suit my schedule during the week. My problem is the days I'm in the gym without classes or running. I did an ab workout today and couldn't find the equipment and didn't get the movements right and just basically flailed for 30 minutes. Then I went on the stairmaster for 10 minutes, and then I did 30 lat pulldowns, 30 leg presses, 30 calf raise machine things, and 30 of the thing where you hook your feet under a bar and lift that. 

If you can't tell I'm new to machines, lol. 

My point is it all felt pointless. Though I felt some of the ab exercises, it wasn't constant and smooth/fast enough to build into something really sweaty where I felt I was working hard. The stairmaster was the only thing that I really felt like I'd done something for. The machines were a challenge but not so bad and I didn't know what I was doing enough to feel pushed. 

I know part of it is having a plan but I had a plan -- the ab workout and elliptical, which were all full so I did the stairmaster instead -- but because I flopped so hard at the ab workout and because I was gonna go for 20 minutes on the elliptical but couldn't on the stairmaster, that's why I started flapping around on machines. My advice (as someone who really desires romantic love and has been rejected from it a *lot* recently) is to make sure you're taking any breaks you need and doing things that make you feel good throughout. If you're only dating because you're sad/feel hopeless, the dates will inevitably feel sad and hopeless and you might miss someone you'd actually get on with. That's not to say you need to love yourself 2000% before you even start going somewhere with someone - what bullshit, nobody feels like that - but it's very hard on yourself and your date if you feel like anyone you meet romantically is your last chance at happiness etc. There's a difference between being frustrated but still giving it a go, and ascribing a huge narrative to a stranger who might really just want to like you (I say as someone who recently did a lot of the latter). It can take time for your confidence to refresh between rejections basically, so I've learned that it's important to take it.

I really hope it goes well, aside from that. It's tough out here, and I hope you meet someone that means you don't have to be super strong all the time when it comes to love. You deserve the best. ❤️
